## IT & Infrastructure Portfolio

This page collects **enterprise IT** and **operations** work: **Active Directory**, **Windows servers**, **help desk ticketing (ITSM)**, and patterns that extend toward **IoT** (device inventory, alerts, and audited changes on gateways and edge hosts).

I hold an **M.S. in Information Technology** (Prince of Songkla University), taught **Programming for Data Science** and led the **Data Science Lab** at ITC, and am completing **CompTIA CySA+** cybersecurity training. Projects here stress **documentation**, **least privilege**, and **ticket-linked changes**—the same habits expected in production IT and security teams.

## Featured article: IT Service Desk & Active Directory Automation Lab

::: {.callout-note}
## Read the full walkthrough

**[IT Service Desk & Active Directory Automation Lab →](../it-service-desk-ad-automation/)**

**Source code:** [github.com/sophalchan/it-service-desk-ad-automation](https://github.com/sophalchan/it-service-desk-ad-automation)
:::

### What this project is (in plain language)

Imagine HR emails: *“Create a login for our new contractor Monday.”* At the same time, monitoring says *“SRV-APP01 CPU is over 90%.”* And another mail: *“Disable the account for someone who left Friday.”* In real companies, these are not three random tasks—they are **tickets** tied to **servers** and **Active Directory accounts**.

This lab lets you practice that workflow on your laptop:

1. **Open a ticket** (who asked, priority, which server, which AD username).  
2. **Do the AD work** (create user, add to VPN group, disable account)—safely using a **mock directory** in SQLite.  
3. **Close the ticket** with a note so auditors see *what* changed and *why*.  
4. **Check a dashboard** (how many open tickets, how many critical, AD vs server breakdown).

When you move to a real Windows domain, the included **PowerShell** scripts mirror the same steps as `New-ADUser` and `Disable-ADAccount`.

### Background of the study

Organizations depend on **Windows Server** (domain controllers, file servers, application servers) and **Active Directory** for logins and security groups. Without a **system of record**, IT work scatters across email and chat: SLAs are missed, offboarding is forgotten, and nobody can prove *which ticket authorized an AD change*.

**IT service management (ITSM)** uses **tickets** as the central object. **Identity lifecycle management** links HR events (hire, transfer, terminate) to AD operations. This project teaches that pattern in a small, runnable stack—useful for **IT/IoT portfolios**, **CySA+** study, or developers moving into **infrastructure operations**.

### Motivation of the study

| Goal | How the lab helps |
|------|-------------------|
| Traceability | Every AD action can reference `ad_sam` and `server_hostname` on the ticket |
| Safe practice | Mock AD on SQLite—no domain controller required for learning |
| Real-world mapping | API routes match `New-ADUser`, `Disable-ADAccount`, `Add-ADGroupMember` |
| Tooling skills | Flask REST API + CLI—same integration style as ServiceNow or Jira |
| Visibility | Dashboard: open queue, critical items, counts by category |

### Sample scenarios in the lab

| Ticket | Category | What you practice |
|--------|----------|-------------------|
| New hire AD account — Engineering | Active Directory | Create SAM account, assign groups (VPN, Engineering) |
| SRV-APP01 high CPU alert | Server | Link ticket to hostname in server inventory |
| Disable AD account — terminated employee | Active Directory | Offboarding: disable account, document in ticket notes |

### Technology stack

| Layer | Tools |
|-------|--------|
| API | Python, Flask (port **8091**) |
| Data | SQLite (`ad_users`, `tickets`, `ticket_notes`) |
| Inventory | `data/servers.json`, `data/ad_users_seed.json` |
| Production AD (optional) | PowerShell in `powershell/` |

### Run it locally (5 minutes)

```bash
git clone https://github.com/sophalchan/it-service-desk-ad-automation.git
cd it-service-desk-ad-automation
python -m venv .venv && source .venv/bin/activate
pip install -r requirements.txt
python scripts/init_lab.py
python app.py
```

```bash
curl http://localhost:8091/dashboard
curl http://localhost:8091/tickets
```

For all API examples, architecture diagram, and step-by-step curl commands, open the **[full project article](../it-service-desk-ad-automation/)**.

## Featured article: Smart Farm Sensor ML (Agriculture IoT)

::: {.callout-tip}
## Read the full walkthrough

**[Smart Farm Sensor ML — Agriculture IoT Analytics →](../smart-farm-sensor-ml/)**

**Source code:** [github.com/sophalchan/smart-farm-sensor-ml](https://github.com/sophalchan/smart-farm-sensor-ml)
:::

**Machine learning on 1,500+ sensor rows** — soil moisture, weather, NPK nutrients, and crop type — to predict **crop stress**, **irrigation need**, and **yield (kg/ha)**. Includes a custom dataset generator, three scikit-learn models, and a Flask prediction API.

```bash
git clone https://github.com/sophalchan/smart-farm-sensor-ml.git
cd smart-farm-sensor-ml && pip install -r requirements.txt
python scripts/run_pipeline.py && python app.py
```

The **[full article](../smart-farm-sensor-ml/)** explains **background of the study** (precision agriculture, IoT, food security) and **motivation** (water efficiency, AgriTech careers, deployable AI).
